key_insight: Africa-Papers introduces an open, 10.15-billion-token academic corpus designed to improve African representation in foundation-model training.
clinical_relevance: Its African medical scholarship may support research on locally relevant clinical language models, but clinical benefits are not demonstrated in the abstract.
method: Combines African journals, CGIAR CGSpace, African-focused arXiv preprints, and OpenAlex-indexed publications.
Converts full texts into layout-aware Markdown preserving sections, equations, and tables.
Adds exact BPE token counts and a standardized eight-domain taxonomy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 844,807 full-text papers across 879 Parquet shards, with the journal stream spanning 31 African nations, but no downstream model or clinical evaluation.
watch_item: Corpus scale alone does not establish balanced coverage or clinical reliability; downstream performance and safety require evaluation.
paper_title: Africa-Papers: A 10-Billion-Token Multi-Domain Academic Corpus for African Foundation Language Models
